object_description: three squat pavilion-like volumes with corner links
design_condition: Three low volumes are placed orthogonally to define outdoor spaces and a central address, while the gymnasium is buried beneath the schoolyard and the site opens toward the surrounding streets.

positive.statement: The precise placement of three squat volumes creates a clear stance in the heterogeneous environment.
The volumes define well-proportioned outdoor spaces as a transition to the surroundings and adjacent buildings.
The two- to three-floor height development creates a pleasant, child-friendly scale.
The central address formation via the break area is convincing.
The outdoor spaces are clearly defined and mesh beautifully with the surroundings.
The partly elevated ground floor allows good lighting on the basement floors.
The consistent wooden structure establishes a clear grid.
The balcony layer is positively assessed for summer heat protection and facade cleaning.

negative.statement: The completely underground gymnasium seems problematic in terms of both use and economic efficiency.
The exposure of the gymnasium below is unclear, and its quality for the gym and break area is questionable.
The pavilion-like buildings are only functionally connected through the outside area and basement, which is impractical for users.
The narrowings between user units on the upper floors appear too limited in space.
The high proportion of glass and the balcony layer raise concerns about mutual insights and disruptions to lessons.
A different height arrangement would have better promoted a playful height development.
